name: codex
title: OpenAI Codex CLI

files.text:
# Written by glov vm create --harness codex.
# A custom provider, because the built-in one tries the Responses WebSocket first, which the glov egress proxy does not
# relay; it then falls back to HTTPS after about 10 s of retries.
model_provider = "glov"
# Commands run in codex's sandbox (the harness VM allows the user namespaces it needs); what needs more, such as the
# network or files outside the workspace, goes to its automatic review instead of a person.
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
approval_policy = "on-request"
approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"
check_for_update_on_startup = false

[model_providers.glov]
name = "OpenAI via glov"
base_url = "https://api.openai.com/v1"
env_key = "CODEX_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
supports_websockets = false

# glov secret login <vm> codex switches model_provider to this one: the ChatGPT sign-in in place of the API key. The
# name "OpenAI" makes codex treat it as its own provider, sent to chatgpt.com, with the WebSocket still off.
[model_providers.glov-chatgpt]
name = "OpenAI"
requires_openai_auth = true
wire_api = "responses"
supports_websockets = false

[analytics]
enabled = false

[feedback]
enabled = false

installScript:
set -eu
d=$(mktemp -d)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/scripts/install/install.sh -o "$d/install.sh"
CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=true CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh "$d/install.sh"
rm -rf "$d"
sudo ln -sf "$HOME/.local/bin/codex" /usr/local/bin/codex
notes: codex exec takes its key from CODEX_API_KEY; OPENAI_API_KEY only pre-fills the sign-in screen.
Statsig metrics (ab.chatgpt.com) and the update check (api.github.com) are off in config.toml, and denied if anything still tries.
ChatGPT sign-in (chatgpt.com) is not allowed: the profile uses the API key, the openai secret, which the egress proxy puts in place of the placeholder.
Observed with the runtime allowlist (0.166.0): codex exec also tries github.com, api.github.com and chatgpt.com, which are denied; the model request still goes through.

The egress proxy does not relay WebSocket upgrades, so config.toml defines a provider with supports_websockets = false; with the built-in openai provider codex exec retries the Responses WebSocket five times before falling back to HTTPS.

Installed with the official installer (the repository's scripts/install/install.sh, which chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh redirects to by way of releases.openai.com) forced to GitHub Releases: the single-binary codex-<target>.tar.gz lacks codex-code-mode-host, without which codex runs no tools.

sandbox_mode = workspace-write, approval_policy = on-request, approvals_reviewer = auto_review: commands run in the bubblewrap sandbox, and escalation requests are approved or denied by the automatic review (extra model calls). The sandbox needs unprivileged user namespaces, which a VM with codex allows (userNamespaces; kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 0); without them it fails with "bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR".
